report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/recipe assistant with a professional/technical cooking orientation (restaurant/chef/kitchen domain).

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly cooking-domain: across mid–late layers and positions 1–4 the top directions point to “Cook”, “Cooking”, “Chef”, “restaurant/Restaurant”, “kitchen”, “baking/Baked/Cake”, “microwave”, “oven”, “culinary”, “Professional/technical”. This clustering is consistent and dominates the highest-norm cells (e.g., L21–L25).
- The signal is strongest at position 1 in later layers (e.g., L21 p1=843, L22 p1=973, L23 p1=1060, L24 p1=1167, L25 p1=1648), suggesting a global steering feature applied right after the start of text, typical of an instruction/domain system objective.
- Earlier layers already show food/food-writing cues alongside academic/technical vocabulary (“culinary”, “Restaurant”, “delectable”, “exquisite”, “Innovation”), and these resolve into unambiguous culinary/pro kitchen tokens in later layers.
- Positions 2–4 consistently rank “professional/Professional” alongside “cooking/restaurant/technical”, pointing to not just casual recipes but a pro/technical culinary style (chef/restaurant context).

Together this indicates the finetune pushes generations toward cooking/recipes and professional kitchen advice rather than general text—i.e., Model B is a chef/culinary assistant.
